en.bdb: The Sikh of the Guru is prideless -

verses.gurmukhi: ਗੋਰਖ ਜਤੀ ਸਦਾਇੰਦਾ ਤਿਸੁ ਗੁਰ ਘਰਬਾਰੀ।
verses.translit_en: gorakh jatee sadhai(n)dhaa tis gur gharabaaree|

en.bdb: Gorakh claimed to be a celebate but his teacher Machhandar (Matsyendr) lived like a virtual householder.
Sukrachary too was stigmatised for his evil mantra.

verses.gurmukhi: ਲਖਮਣ ਸਾਧੀ ਭੁਖ ਤੇਹ ਹਉਮੈ ਅਹੰਕਾਰੀ।
verses.translit_en: lakhaman saadhee bhukh teh haumai aha(n)kaaree|

en.bdb: Laksaman disciplined his hunger and thirst and was proud on this account.

verses.gurmukhi: ਹਨੂੰਮਾਨ ਬਲਵੰਤ ਹੋਇ ਚੰਚਲ ਮਤਿ ਖਾਰੀ।
verses.translit_en: hanoo(n)maan balava(n)t hoi cha(n)chal mat khaaree|

en.bdb: Hanumán (monkey god) is known to be very powerful but his mind was quite volatile.

verses.gurmukhi: ਭੈਰਉ ਭੂਤ ਕੁਸੂਤ ਸੰਗਿ ਦੁਰਮਤਿ ਉਰਧਾਰੀ।
verses.translit_en: bhairau bhoot kusoot sa(n)g dhuramat uradhaaree|

en.bdb: Bhairav also because of his association with evil spirits maintained his evilmindedness.

verses.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਸਿਖ ਜਤੀ ਸਲਾਹੀਅਨਿ ਜਿਨਿ ਹਉਮੈ ਮਾਰੀ ॥੭॥
verses.translit_en: gursikh jatee salaaheean jin haumai maaree ||7||

en.bdb: Sikhs of the Guru who have effaced their ego are praised as (really) virtuous persons.
